th Order No. 03/Dated: 08 September, 2025
1. Heard Mr. Sunil Singh, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. Vishwanath Roy, learned Spl.P.P. for the State.
2. This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.

3. The appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Section 376 (2)(n) of the I.P.C. and Section 6 of the POCSO Act and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for a period of 21 years along with fine of Rs. 25,000/- for the offence under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
4. It has been alleged that on the pretext of marriage, the appellant has established physical relation with the daughter of the informant.

5. Submission has been advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant that the victim has admitted that there was love affairs between victim and the appellant, which resulted in establishment of physical relationship between them.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that appellant is in custody since 21.02.2023.
7. Learned Spl.P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.

8. It appears that the appellant is a married person, having three children and despite the said fact,
he had promised marriage to the victim and taking advantage of the same had established physical relationship with the victim.
The victim admittedly was a minor at the time of the incident.
9. Regard being had to the above, we are not inclined to grant bail to the appellant.
The prayer for bail of the appellant is hereby rejected.

(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) (Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Sunil/
